title: Characterisation of protein deposit layers on polyethersulphone membranes by atomic force microscopy and confocal laser scanning microscopy

record.title: Characterisation of protein deposit layers on polyethersulphone membranes by atomic force microscopy and confocal laser scanning microscopy
record.abstract: Protein deposit layers formed during ultrafiltration of bovine serum albumin (BSA) and β-lactoglobulin solutions were characterised by atomic force microscopy (AFM) and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM). Membranes with nominal molecular weight cut-offs of 10, 30, and 50 kDa were fouled at constant transmembrane pressures of 1.5 and 3.0 bar. AFM height images revealed root-mean-square roughness values of 38–112 nm for fouled surfaces compared with 6–14 nm for clean membranes. CLSM cross-sections using fluorescently labelled BSA showed deposit thicknesses of 2–8 µm depending on operating pressure and protein concentration. Adhesion force measurements by AFM colloidal probe technique indicated protein–membrane adhesion forces of 1.2–4.7 nN, with the 10 kDa membrane showing the highest adhesion. These data support mechanistic fouling models that distinguish surface coverage from pore blockage.
